items.title: TASK-010 — Platform red-flag correction feedback
items.outcome: Any eligible data cell or bullet supports one subtle, scoped, reversible red-flag correction that feeds governed learning.
items.prototypeTest: Hover/focus a cell and bullet, flag each, explain scope, undo it, inspect the audit evidence, and verify no green/yellow feedback semantics remain.
evidence: [TASK-010 round-1 output](../outputs/2026-07-17-task010-red-flag-feedback.md), [round-2/3 remediation](../outputs/2026-07-17-task010-review-remediation.md), [round-4 remediation](../outputs/2026-07-17-task010-round4-remediation.md) — shared `RedFlagControl` primitive wired into TableView.tsx (data cells) and JobPilotApplicationDetail.tsx (rendered bullets), plus a Settings > Learning "Red flags" audit section

DealPilot/JobPilot green/yellow/red flag semantics removed (AP-023). Three coordinator-directed independent reviews found defects, all now remediated: round 1's auth/IDOR, ledger-privacy, saga/idempotency, CAS/lineage, anchor-identity, pagination, N+1, and touch-detection gaps (round 2)
round 2's own idempotency-check and CAS `.cause`-unwrap bugs (round 3)

and round 4's 11-item list — **governed learning is now substantive, not an echo**: `create` synthesizes a real, structured, owner-private `preference_adjustment` Memory (scope/target/proposed-change/rationale/evidence-ref) via owner-authorized read, and a SEPARATE Human-authorized `enactCorrection`/`revokeCorrection` pair applies/undoes the actual correction (display suppression) only after ledger approval — proving "behavior changes only after approval and can be undone"

**private-proposal ownership** — `action.listPending`/`decide` now hide/reject a red-flag's private proposal from every non-owner member while preserving full team-visible semantics for unrelated proposals
**replay-safe create** — reconciles against the ledger before re-proposing (crash recovery lands on "proposed" not "failed"), and a genuinely failed attempt is retryable

**durable clear/reopen** — withdrawal/revocation happens BEFORE the status flip (a failure leaves the flag untouched, safely retryable), and reopen mints a FRESH proposal rather than resurrecting a resolved one
**forget** enumerates and withdraws every proposal across the WHOLE lineage, not just the current head's
**server-validated canonical anchors** — JobPilot/DealPilot/People/Community/Touchpoint record targets are existence+workspace-checked server-side (unknown modules fail closed)
**DB-pushed scope/kind filtering** via a new `MemoryQuery.contentPathEquals` JSON-predicate mechanism (no migration)
**real keyset `(createdAt,id)` pagination** replaces offset-based `listAll`/`history`, removing the 200-version cap

and JobPilot's legacy `flag` column is normalized at the `DrizzleJobPilotStore` read boundary itself (every `createJob`/`listJobs`/`updateApplication`/`getApplication` call), not only a test helper. Round 4 also found and fixed 3 further real bugs while implementing: a stale `.get(id)` (vs. `currentForLineage`) read of the preference-adjustment lineage after `enactCorrection` superseded it
a non-monotonic outcome-Memory id causing a primary-key collision on any retry that changed learning status

and every superseding write silently inheriting its PREDECESSOR's `createdAt` via `{...current}` spread (broke history/keyset ordering) — fixed via a process-local monotonic timestamp helper. Re-verified: core 426, DB 118, API 203 (33 red-flag tests), JobPilot 94, DealPilot 72, Commons 22, integrations-google 35, web 59 tests, full monorepo build (23/23 packages) and typecheck clean, lint clean, no-dummy-runtime clean. Item 9/11's JobPilot flag-column migration remains explicitly PENDING (not fabricated) — TASK-008 RM4 owns migration 0015 and has not landed. A pre-existing, unrelated dummy-data instance (`JobPilotApplicationDetail.tsx`'s unrouted `BCG_APPLICATION` fixture) was discovered and logged to `docs/dummy.md` rather than silently left untracked. Outstanding before this task can close: live desktop+375px browser evidence of the actual hover/focus/click/touch interaction, and the pending RM4-dependent migration.

items.title: TASK-021 — Task Manager Module
items.outcome: One installable Task Manager Module owning the single governed execution queue per workspace as ONE self-referential, dot-path-leveled Task type (no separate Goal/Initiative/Outcome Record types — `is_goal` is a field, not a type), with full tree restructuring (promote/insert-ancestor-above/re-parent) as governed proposals, exit-test verification with reopenable done/archived/parked status, planning Playbooks as draft-then-approve proposals, no-default agent-task routing owned by Chief of Staff, confidence-graduated reschedule and routing approval, proactive cross-Module opportunity scanning, guard Automations, and an agent-first `tasks.md` ledger projection consumable by external coding agents.
items.prototypeTest: In a real workspace, create a goal-flagged Task (`is_goal=true`) with outcomes[] and a 3-level Task tree under it (paths e.g. `1`, `1.1`, `1.1.1`) with exit tests via UI; creating a new Task against a populated queue produces an Internal-Strategist impact-fit/resequence proposal before it settles; promoting `1.1.1` to a new root (path recomputes, old ancestor untouched) and inserting a new ancestor above an existing branch both round-trip as approved proposals with correct path recomputation; an agent-assigned Task routes to whichever eligible Agent owns its required Skill (Chief of Staff resolves, no default — Capability Builder only when genuinely a capability/code Task) and an ambiguous Task escalates to explicit Human assignment; a human reschedule proposal requires approval, then a minor-banded reschedule auto-applies only after calibration while a significant one still requires approval; a done Task is reopened to pending after its outcome target changes; the projected tasks.md round-trips an external edit through drift-detect→reconcile without silent overwrite; a done-without-evidence task is reopened by the challenger; the game-designs instance's coding agent works one full task (orient→execute→evidence→done→sweep) from the projected ledger.
